context: Daichi gives Sho-young some tips on running a marathon.

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.jp: 翔、ランナー、よくよく見てみ。
lines.en: Sho — look closely at that runner over there.
lines.style: Warm, encouraging Kansai father-voice. Soft opening, drawing his attention gently. Genuinely proud of what he's about to show his son. Conversational, never lecturing.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.style: Pure awe from a six-year-old. Small, genuine brightness. Eyes wide. Steady tone, no performance, just honest amazement at what he's seeing.

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.jp: がんばる姿勢、深く、感じるな。
lines.en: See how hard they're trying? Feel that effort.
lines.style: Soft, reverent Kansai register. Gentle hand maybe on Sho's shoulder. Speaking as much to himself as to his son — inviting rather than instructing. Slow enough to let the moment land.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: 直ぐに、止まらず、続けてる!
lines.en: They're not stopping — they keep going!
lines.style: Quiet appreciation, building slightly. Still soft but with a little more energy now — Sho's recognizing something real about persistence. No big gestures, just noticing aloud.

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.jp: 焦らず、ペース、保つのが大事や。
lines.en: Not rushing it — keeping the right pace, that's what matters.
lines.style: Gentle wisdom from a father who means it. Slow pace, room between phrases. Not preachy — just steady truth. The tone of someone who's learned this the hard way.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.en: Come on, let's cheer them on!
lines.style: Suddenly bright and animated. Energy lifts naturally — inviting Sho in, not pushing. Warm Kansai brightness. The 'let's' matters — they're doing this together.

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.style: Full-throated, generous father-shout. Unselfconscious joy. Loud enough to carry but not harsh — the kind of cheer that makes people feel genuinely seen. Daichi's affection on full display.
